reasoning.text: Base-rate/reference-class anchor: the comparable complete monthly CPI annual readings since late 2025 are clustered around 3.4% to 4.6%, with the latest three prints at 4.6%, 4.2%, and 4.0%. A simple latest-value prior starts at 4.0%, but the June 2025 base month was a low 0.1%, so a normal positive June 2026 month lifts the annual rate mechanically.

Level and momentum: May's -0.7% monthly fall pulled the headline annual rate down despite still-firm housing and underlying inflation. I treat part of that May drop, especially transport and recreation, as likely to mean-revert rather than persist fully into June.

One-off and policy mechanisms: housing remains the main upside channel because May Housing was 6.5% year over year and electricity was affected by rebate timing, while automotive fuel and travel prices are the main downside-or-rebound channels after May Transport fell 3.9% month over month.

Prior/update/interval: prior model is latest-value annual CPI persistence with a base-month bridge, using the official monthly sample from June 2025 through May 2026 and the latest annual prints of 4.6%, 4.2%, and 4.0%. Adjustment components are +0.4 pp for replacing June 2025's 0.1% base with an assumed roughly 0.5% June 2026 month, +0.1 pp for rebound from May's temporary transport/recreation weakness, and -0.1 pp for trimmed-mean restraint near 3.6%. The 80% interval maps a realized monthly first-print range of about -0.2% to +1.1% for June 2026 through the same annual-rate bridge, rounded to final implied bounds of 3.7% to 5.0%.

Annual-rate bridge from May: May annual CPI 4.0% implies index ratio 1.040 versus May 2025. Using June 2025 monthly CPI 0.1% and a central June 2026 monthly CPI of 0.5%, the implied June annual rate is 1.040 * 1.005 / 1.001 - 1 = 0.0442, or 4.4% after one-decimal rounding. For the interval, June 2026 monthly outcomes from about -0.2% to +1.1% imply roughly 3.7% to 5.0% after rounding.

Counter-consideration: if May's fuel and travel weakness continues rather than reverses, the release could remain near 4.0% or below despite the low June 2025 base; conversely, an electricity or fuel rebound could push headline inflation materially above the underlying trend.

Outside-the-interval scenarios: below 3.7% would likely require another broad monthly fall led by fuel, airfares, or goods discounting; above 5.0% would likely require a large June price jump from electricity, fuel, rents, or a travel-price rebound coinciding with little offset elsewhere.
